assertion_results.text: States that jwt.decode does not verify the signature (token is forgeable) — distinct from just 'trusting the role claim'
assertion_results.evidence: "`jwt.decode` reads the token without checking its signature, so anyone can make themselves admin."

assertion_results.text: Describes the exploit: forge/modify a token to role=admin (or alg=none) to bypass auth
assertion_results.evidence: "the attacker writes their own token, `base64url({"alg":"none"}).base64url({"role":"admin"}).`, or any token with a made-up signature, and sends it"

assertion_results.text: Fix: verify the signature with jwt.verify (key + expiry) before trusting any claim
assertion_results.evidence: "Use `jwt.verify(token, key, { algorithms: ['RS256'], issuer, audience })`... Let `verify` enforce `exp`/`nbf`."

assertion_results.text: Rates it Critical/High and follows the exploit + impact + fix format
assertion_results.evidence: Under "🔴 Must fix": "Exploit: the attacker writes their own token... · Impact: any unauthenticated user gets full admin access. → Use `jwt.verify(...)`"
